internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The consonantal skeleton ذ ن ب hosts two Quran-internally unbridged noun lexemes, not one nucleus. Class 1 (ذَنْب faʿl singular + ذُنُوب fuʿūl plural, 37 occ) is uniformly an imputable culpable act that grounds liability: it is what is forgiven (ghafara/istaghfara), invoked as the causal ground of seizure/destruction/punishment (bi-ḏanbihim), confessed (iʿtarafa bi-), and interrogated/known-about (yusʾalu ʿan, khabīr bi-). Class 2 (ذَنُوب faʿūl singular, only 51:59, twice) is directionally opposite: an allotted portion/measure received BY the wrongdoers (li-lladhīna ẓalamū ḏanūban), matched (miṯl) to their predecessors' and something they might wish hastened (yastaʿjilūn) — an effect handed to them, not a cause they commit. Because the only conceivable bridge (a concrete 'tail/that-which-trails' substrate) is nowhere attested in the packet and would require an external lexical prior, and because forcing 'sin' onto 51:59 breaks the āya, the honest root-level verdict is a two-class partition with no demonstrated bridge. Class 1 is internally CONSISTENT as a lexeme; the root as a whole is UNRESOLVED.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Within Class 1, dhanb does NOT denote the punishment itself: it is the bi- causal ground, coordinated against ʿiqāb (3:11:11:2 bi-ḏunūbihim … shadīd al-ʿiqāb) and against ʿadhāb (3:16:8:1 ḏunūbanā … ʿadhāb al-nār). dhanb is NOT co-extensive with generic wrongdoing: it is coordinated alongside sayyiʾāt (3:193:14:1, distinct verb kaffara) and isrāf (3:147:10:1), so non-synonymous with either. dhanb is NOT the agent-label (khāṭiʾ 12:29, mujrim 28:78 sit in separate slots). dhanb does NOT entail actual moral guilt — 81:9:2:1 presupposes its absence for the buried infant, and 26:14:3:1 is a charge held against Moses in an accuser's frame. Number (singular vs plural) is NOT a semantic split: parallel frames occur in both. Class 2 dhanūb does NOT belong to this accountability frame at all and must not be glossed as 'sin' or assimilated to Class 1.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 51:59 (ذَنُوبًا / ذَنُوبِ): 'fa-inna lilladhīna ẓalamū ḏanūban miṯla ḏanūbi aṣḥābihim fa-lā yastaʿjilūn' — a faʿūl lexeme distinct from the faʿl/fuʿūl of Class 1, functioning as an allotted portion RECEIVED by the wrongdoers (dative lām of what is due, comparison miṯl to predecessors, and yastaʿjilūn marking a coming measured lot), i.e. the effect/consequence, the polar inverse of Class 1's dhanb which is the committed cause invoked against a bearer (bi-ḏanbihim). Substituting 'sin' collapses the āya (the wrongdoers already sinned, and one does not hasten a sin). No packet occurrence uses ḏanūb and ḏanb in a shared or punning frame, so the two classes cannot be bridged from packet-internal evidence.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: A unifying 'that-which-trails / consequence' account: the offense as the deed that trails behind and returns (Class 1) and the trailing portion of doom (Class 2), reduced to one abstract nucleus. Rejected on two Quran-internal grounds: (1) it requires the external etymon dhanab='tail', which is forbidden and is nowhere attested in the 39 occurrences in any bare follow/trail sense; (2) it fails on its own terms because to cover both classes the single gloss must invert cause↔effect (Class 1 dhanb is the ground OF the consequence via bi-; Class 2 dhanūb IS the consequence via lām), which is exactly the vague abstraction-that-fits-everything the methodology rejects as non-useful.

Forcing a single 'sin' nucleus over all 39 would be the exact failure caught at 51:59.
